headline: US says it has escorted 1 billion barrels of crude oil out of Hormuz
summary: The United States says more than 2,000 commercial vessels have crossed the Strait of Hormuz under protection and that the main routes are free of mines. The claim concerns roughly 1 billion barrels of crude oil.
why: The Strait of Hormuz carries a large share of the world's seaborne oil, so shipping disruptions there feed directly into crude prices and supply expectations.
why_moved: Reported escorted tanker traffic and mine-free routes bear on expectations for crude flows out of the Gulf. The input does not give a price reaction.
